slice: For a sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on a topos $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$, the slice $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})/\mathcal{F}$ is a topos. The localization morphism $j_{\mathcal{F}}$ has inverse image $\mathcal{H}\mapsto(\mathcal{H}\times\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F})$ and left adjoint forgetting the map to $\mathcal{F}$. A topos morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})$ induces a localized morphism over an object $\mathcal{G}$ of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})$, whose inverse image applies $f^{-1}$ to objects over $\mathcal{G}$. For representable $\mathcal{F}=h_U^\#$, the slice identifies with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}/U)$.
point: For a site $\mathcal{C}$ and functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\textit{Sets}$, its category of neighbourhoods has objects $(U,x)$, $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})$, $x\in u(U)$, with morphisms $\alpha:(V,y)\to(U,x)$ satisfying $u(\alpha)(y)=x$. Define the stalk of a presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ at $p=u$ by $\mathcal{F}_p=\operatorname{colim}_{(U,x)^{opp}}\mathcal{F}(U)$. The functor $u^p:\textit{Sets}\to\operatorname{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$ sends a set $E$ to $U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(u(U),E)$. A point of the site additionally satisfies local surjectivity, pullback bijectivity on coverings, and left-exactness of the stalk functor.
point_power: Let $p=u:\mathcal{C}\to\textit{Sets}$ be a point of a site and take an infinite set $S_0$ containing each set $u(U)$ as a subset. Let $S=\mathcal{P}(S_0)$ and make $\mathcal{S}$ the category whose objects are subsets of $S_0$ and whose morphisms are all functions of sets. Give $\mathcal{S}$ a site structure by a suitable set of jointly surjective covering families. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{S})$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Sh}(pt)=\textit{Sets}$, with inverse image given by evaluation at a singleton object $e$ and direct image $E\mapsto(T\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(T,E))$. The point $p$ gives a morphism of topoi $(p_*,p^{-1})$ with $p^{-1}\mathcal{F}=\mathcal{F}_p$ and $p_*E=U\mapsto\operatorname{Map}(u(U),E)$ as a sheaf.
locpoint: For a site point $p=u:\mathcal{C}\to\textit{Sets}$, object $U$, and element $x\in u(U)$, define a functor $q_x:\mathcal{C}/U\to\textit{Sets}$ by $q_x(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)=\{y\in u(V):u(\varphi)(y)=x\}$. It is a point of the localized site and lies over $p$ under the localization morphism $j_U:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}/U)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$. For any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$, $(j_U^{-1}\mathcal{F})_{q_x}=\mathcal{F}_p$ whenever this point is specified.
